disease_label_per_paper: Odontogenic orbital cellulitis with orbital abscess
presentation_summary: A 40-year-old man presented with 12 hours of rapidly progressive right facial pain, eyelid swelling, and visual loss.
Detailed history found a right maxillary toothache that began 3 days earlier.
At presentation he reported diplopia, restricted right eye motility, and pain worsened by eye movement; he was afebrile.
Exam showed right periorbital and facial edema, ptosis, proptosis, slight exotropia, visual acuity 20/60, intraocular pressure 16 mm Hg, and no afferent pupillary defect.
Admission labs showed WBC 8.5 x10^9/L with 13% bands.

Admission CT showed bilateral periapical lucency, superior alveolar ridge inflammation, breakdown of the right maxillary sinus base, right proptosis, orbital inflammation, and orbital emphysema adjacent to the right inferior rectus muscle.

risk_context.source_text_value: right maxillary toothache 3 days earlier; CT periapical lucency and dental infection

risk_context.factor: visual compromise, RAPD, severe proptosis, or ophthalmoplegia at presentation

hospital day 4 CT showed a 24 x 18 x 21 mm orbital abscess indistinguishable from the right inferior rectus muscle

microbiology.source_text_value: wound culture was positive for anaerobic gram-positive cocci

procedures.source_text_value: right second and third molars were extracted on hospital day 2
urgent right orbitotomy for incision and drainage of the right orbital abscess

actual_treatment.name: right second and third molar extraction on hospital day 2
urgent right orbitotomy with incision and drainage on hospital day 4

clinical_course.description: Facial swelling, proptosis, and ptosis improved after antibiotics and molar extraction, but eye pain and diplopia persisted.
He developed increasing fever, chills, worsening eye pain, WBC 17.0 x10^9/L, visual acuity 20/200, and CT-confirmed orbital abscess.

clinical_course.source_text_value: moderate leukocytosis of 17,000 white blood cells

outcome_follow_up.description: Postoperative imaging showed no residual inflammation.
Three weeks after discharge, proptosis and diplopia completely resolved and right eye vision returned to 20/20.

quality_warnings: Orbital abscess, wound culture, molar extraction, orbitotomy, and treatment response are saved as post-presentation evidence with use_in_ranking:false.
Initial afebrile presentation and normal-range WBC with bandemia are preserved rather than altered.
